instructions: Butter a 9 by 9 inch baking dish with 1 tbsp of the butter and line it with parchment.
Melt the remaining 8 tbsp butter in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add 6 cups of the marshmallows and stir until they're melted and smooth. Don't let them scorch.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the vanilla and the salt.
Fold in the cereal, then the remaining 2 cups marshmallows. Stir just until the cereal is coated and the new marshmallows begin to soften but stay chunky.
Transfer the mixture to the pan, cover it with parchment or plastic wrap and press it into an even layer.
Let it cool to room temperature, about 1 hour, then cut it into 16 squares.
Keep the squares in an airtight container at room temperature for 2 days, or freeze them in layers with wax paper between for up to 6 weeks. Let frozen squares stand for 15 minutes before serving.
method_notes: The sources agree on melting butter, stirring in marshmallows, folding in the cereal and pressing it into a pan. Sugar Spun Run saves some marshmallows to fold in at the end for gooey pockets, and adds vanilla and salt; Kellogg's original uses 3 tbsp butter and a 13 by 9 pan. I followed Sugar Spun Run (4.94 from 175 votes) and used gelatin-free marshmallows so it stays vegetarian. Storage times are from Kellogg's.
